'''Amber Lynn Puha''' is an American mathematician and educator at [[California State University San Marcos]]. Her research concerns probability theory and stochastic processes.<ref name="csusm_profile">{{Cite web |title=Amber Puha, PhD {{!}} CSUSM |url=https://faculty.csusm.edu/apuha/ |access-date=2022-04-20 |website=faculty.csusm.edu}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
She earned a B.A. in mathematics at [[University of California, San Diego]] (UCSD) in 1993 and a Ph.D. in mathematics at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) under the supervision of [[Thomas M. Liggett]] in 1998.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amber Puha - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=36639 |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

== Career ==
She joined [[California State University San Marcos]] (CSUSM) in 1999. She was appointed an associate professor in 2005 and a full professor in 2010. She has been the chair of the Department of Mathematics at CSUSM since 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty Directory {{!}} Department of Mathematics {{!}} CSUSM |url=https://www.csusm.edu/math/facultylist.html |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=www.csusm.edu}}</ref>

Her research has been focused on the modeling and analysis of stochastic networks.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Puha |first1=Amber |title=Critical Exponents for a Reversible Nearest Particle System on the Binary Tree |journal=The Annals of Probability |date=2000 |volume=28 |doi=10.1214/aop/1019160124 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Puha |first1=Amber |last2=Alexander |first2=Stolyar |last3=Ruth |first3=Williams |title=The Fluid Limit of an Overloaded Processor Sharing Queue |journal=[[Mathematics of Operations Research]] |date=2006 |volume=31 |issue=2 |pages=316–350 |doi=10.1287/moor.1050.0181 |doi-access=}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Down |first1=Douglas |last2=Gromoll |first2=H. Christian |last3=Puha |first3=Amber |title=Fluid Limits for Shortest Remaining Processing Time Queues |journal=[[Mathematics of Operations Research]] |date=2009 |volume=34 |issue=4 |pages=880–911 |doi=10.1287/moor.1090.0409 |doi-access=}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Down |first1=Douglas |last2=Gromoll |first2=H. Jointly with H. Christian Gromoll and [[Ruth J. Williams]], she developed fluid ([[law of large numbers]]) and diffusion ([[central limit theorem]]) approximations for processor sharing queues with renewal arrivals and iid service requirements.<ref>{{Cite journal|first1=H. Christian|last1=Gromoll|first2=Amber|last2=Puha|first3=Ruth|last3=Williams|date=2002|title=The fluid limit of a heavily loaded processor sharing queue|journal=The Annals of Applied Probability|volume=12 |issue=3 |doi=10.1214/aoap/1031863171|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Puha|first1=Amber|last2=Williams|first2=Ruth|date=2004|title=Invariant states and rates of convergence for a critical fluid model of a processor sharing queue|journal=The Annals of Applied Probability|volume=14 |issue=2 |doi=10.1214/105051604000000017|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0405289}}</ref> By removing the Poisson arrival and the exponential service assumptions in previous literatures, this work advanced the state of art of applied probability and has board applications, "from many-server parallel queues that model call centers to bandwidth sharing communications networks that model the Internet."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dai |first1=J.G. “Jim” |last2=Taylor |first2=Peter |last3=Mandelbaum |first3=Avishai |title=INFORMS 2007 Best Publication Award Citation |url=https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/INFORMS/50069173-2ea8-479b-baa7-2071ed7cd5dc/UploadedImages/Bestpub_2007.doc |access-date=6 May 2022}}</ref>

===Professional services===
From 2009 to 2011, she served as an associate director at the [[Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics]], a federally funded mathematics research institute on the UCLA campus. From 2013 to 2015, she served a three-year elected term on the [[American Mathematical Society]] Council, the main governing body of the society.<ref>{{cite web |title=Council Past Members |url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/council-past.html |website=AMS |access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref> From 2016 to 2019, she served on the [[INFORMS]] Applied Probability Society Prize Committee.<ref>{{cite web |title=Previous Prize Selection Committee Members |url=https://connect.informs.org/aps/about-us/apsofficers/previousprizecommittees |website=INFORMS |access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref> From 2017 to 2020, she served on the Committee On Travel Awards of the Institute for Mathematical Statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} Past Committee Members |url=https://imstat.org/past-committee-members/ |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=imstat.org |language=en}}</ref> Since 2013, she has been the coordinator of The Southern California Probability Symposium, an annual gathering of probabilists supported by [[University of California, Irvine]], [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], [[University of California, Santa Barbara|UCSB]], [[University of California, San Diego|UCSD]], and [[University of Southern California]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SoCal Probability |url=https://scps.pstat.ucsb.edu/history.html |access-date=2022-04-20 |website=scps.pstat.ucsb.edu}}</ref>

Since 2019, she has been an associate editor of ''[[Mathematics of Operations Research]]'' in the area of stochastic models.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editorial Board {{!}} Mathematics of Operations Research |url=https://pubsonline.informs.org/page/moor/editorial-board |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=pubsonline.informs.org |language=en}}</ref>

From 2013-2015, Puha served as a Council Member at Large for the American Mathematical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> Since 2016, she has been a life member at American Mathematical Society. 

===Other services===
In addition to her academic work, she served as the faculty advisor for the CSUSM Surf Team, which competes in the [[National Scholastic Surfing Association]] (NSSA). She led the team to its first and second National Championship in 2009<ref>{{cite web |last1=Aragon |first1=Janice |title=2009 NSSA NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP WRAP UP AND RESULTS! |url=http://www.nssa.org/newsmanager/templates/NSSAArticle.aspx?articleid=633&zoneid=8 |website=NSSA |access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref> and 2019,<ref>{{cite web |last1=NSSA |title=2019 NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP RESULTS! |url=http://www.nssa.org/newsmanager/templates/NSSAArticle.aspx?articleid=1431&zoneid=1 |website=NSSA |access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref> respectively. She won the NSSA Coach of the Year award in 2019.

Williams]]<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Best Publication Award: Past Winners |url=https://connect.informs.org/aps/apsawards/bestpub-past |website=INFORMS |access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref>
* Greater San Diego Area Mathematics Council Outstanding Post Secondary Mathematics Teacher (2009)<ref name="csusm_profile"></ref>
* CSUSM Presidents Outstanding Faculty Award for Scholarship and Creative Activity (2015/2016)<ref>{{cite web |title=Previous Awardees: President's Outstanding Faculty Awards |url=https://www.csusm.edu/president/awards/outstandingfaculty/previousawardees.html |website=CSUSM |access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref>
* National Scholastic Surfing Association Coach of the Year (2019)<ref name="csusm_profile"></ref>
